predecessors.name: Shang dynasty
predecessors.text: Deng, placed at Xiangfan (Xiangyang), Hubei; the page's infobox also offers Dengzhou, Henan: 'Sources conflict as to whether the State of Deng was situated in' Dengzhou or Xiangfan

successors.name: Chu
successors.text: Deng, placed at Xiangfan (Xiangyang), Hubei; the page's infobox also offers Dengzhou, Henan: 'Sources conflict as to whether the State of Deng was situated in' Dengzhou or Xiangfan

ledger.x: c. 1200 BC: the Shang king Wu Ding gives the lands of Deng to his younger brother Zi Man. Infobox 'Established: c. 1200 BCE'; 'Shang King Wu Ding conferred the lands of the State of Deng on his younger brother Zĭ Màn' (Wu Ding 'reigned 1250-1192 BCE'), so the year is the infobox's round figure and the site is the…
678: the state of Deng ends in Chu's conquest; its people afterwards 'adopted the surname Deng'.

wars.name: Chu conquest of Deng
wars.outcome: King Wen of Chu conquered Deng in 678 BC and annexed it; Chu's territory then reached the Nanyang Basin.

certainty.note: No Deng boundary is on the page; the site itself is disputed between Dengzhou and Xiangfan.
